### Module(s)

Completion

### Description

When I select a mini.completion item, the Roslyn language server immediately crashes, and mini.completion then throws errors because the client disappears. This doesn't happen for nvim-cmp, and the crash is from a null check on the data passed to the LS.

LSP Logs
```

```
Source of crash
```csharp
private static LSP.TextDocumentIdentifier? GetTextDocumentCacheEntry(LSP.CompletionItem request)
{
    Contract.ThrowIfNull(request.Data); // <- This is null for some reason.
    var resolveData = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<DocumentResolveData>((JsonElement)request.Data);
    if (resolveData is null)
    {
        Contract.Fail("Document should always be provided when resolving a completion item request.");
        return null;
    }

    return resolveData.TextDocument;
}
```
Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/475d411a-d109-4748-b936-1f90f9a3c203




### Neovim version

0.10.2

### Steps to reproduce

1) Install [seblj/roslyn](https://github.com/seblj/roslyn.nvim)
2) Install mini.completion
3) Open a completion item in a C# file

### Expected behavior

The item's documentation is shown (if any).

### Actual behavior

The language server crashes.

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

This doesn't look like an issue in 'mini.completion'. At least for the following reasons:
- Although error manifests itself in 'mini.completion', the core issue is that LSP server seems to stop after (what should be) a valid request for a item documentation via `completionItem/resolve` request. Later it tries to cancel it in a proper way (via calling output of `vim.lsp.buf_request_all()`) but client has already stopped and hence the error. As other servers do not stop in this situation, I'd assume it is not a 'mini.completion' fault.
- There is another plugin ('seblj/roslyn.nvim') at play here which might affect client-server interactions.

Closing as (most probably) not a 'mini.completion' issue but somewhere upstream ('seblj/roslyn.nvim', Neovim's `vim.lsp.buf_request_all()`, LSP server itself).

labels.description: Related to how upstream application works
labels.name: upstream
